tasks.short: Investigate water storage, discharge or compliance issues

steps.what: Define the actual water investigation question and evidence needed
inputs: actual water storage, discharge, pollution or permit concern

steps.what: Review current permit records, site history and actual water monitoring results
inputs: existing actual monitoring results with location, time, method and units
outputs: checked existing evidence and missing information

steps.what: Conduct the actual site investigation or oversee staff collecting required water evidence
inputs: checked existing evidence and missing information
actual site conditions and staff findings
outputs: actual investigation observations and evidence limitations

steps.what: Capture actual observations and verified staff evidence with source references
inputs: actual investigation observations and evidence limitations

steps.what: Evaluate the actual evidence and write justified findings and unresolved regulatory questions
inputs: checked existing evidence and missing information

steps.what: Assemble the investigation report from verified evidence and actual findings
Approve the completed investigation report after checking source support and limits
Save the approved investigation report in the case record

tasks.design: Configure monitoring and case views in the water records system {OPS_SYSTEM} and an evidence-linked report template in {DOCS}. The specialist conducts or oversees the actual investigation, captures findings and judges the evidence; configuration reduces retrieval and assembly only.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reviewing existing monitoring records and assembling a source-linked report can add work around an investigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native location/time filters and report templates can reuse actual records without creating observations.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete sampling, conflicting evidence and permit applicability require competent human judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist recognises when available records do not answer the actual site question.

ambition.what: Revisit an investigation when new verified monitoring evidence arrives.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2–5 for site records, field access and staff consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: water monitoring records can be filtered by site and time and reused in evidence-linked document templates.

assumptions: Shares and savings are provisional scenario arithmetic, not measured investigation baselines.
Existing monitoring results have actual locations, times, methods and units. New field work remains in s3 and actual capture in s4; missing laboratory work is not free.
Native filters and templates first; findings and regulatory interpretation remain human.
No external regulatory submission is assumed merely because an internal investigation report exists. Same-system save has no saving.
unknowns: Coverage and traceability of monitoring records
research_questions: Which source-retrieval and report-assembly work remains after native configuration?

already_counted.description: Check the completed investigation report against actual evidence

incremental.description: Maintain monitoring filters and case-report source mappings

approvals.approved_version: approved final water investigation report; edits return to s7

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross is 7.5 retrieval hours +4 assembly hours =11.5. Upkeep 1.5 gives central net 10%; three extra hours resolving mismatched monitoring records gives high 7%. Low zero if native workflows already cover this work.

steps.what: Define actual water supply, conservation and compliance goals and binding constraints
inputs: current applicable permit and operating constraints

steps.what: Discuss actual operational options and trade-offs with watershed operators and affected colleagues
inputs: participants' actual operating limits and concerns
outputs: human-defined operating options and actual stakeholder constraints

steps.what: Check actual watershed supply, demand, quality and conservation data for the planning period
inputs: existing actual watershed monitoring and demand records
human-defined operating options and actual stakeholder constraints
outputs: checked strategy dataset with explicit uncertainty and gaps

steps.what: Run approved watershed operating scenarios and inspect supply and conservation outcomes
inputs: checked strategy dataset with explicit uncertainty and gaps
human-defined operating options and actual stakeholder constraints
validated watershed model and approved scenario assumptions
outputs: reproducible scenario outcomes with assumptions and sensitivity limits

steps.what: Choose a defensible watershed operations strategy and explain its trade-offs and unresolved risks
inputs: reproducible scenario outcomes with assumptions and sensitivity limits
human-defined operating options and actual stakeholder constraints

steps.what: Prepare the strategy plan from the chosen rationale, scenario results and actual operating conditions
inputs: reproducible scenario outcomes with assumptions and sensitivity limits

steps.what: Approve the completed strategy plan against its source assumptions and chosen goals
Save the approved proposed watershed strategy

tasks.design: Configure watershed data views in {DATA_PLATFORM} and reusable scenarios in the existing hydrological planning application {OTHER}. A template in {DOCS} carries the results and human-chosen rationale into a proposed strategy; it does not issue operating commands or decide compliance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated data preparation, scenario setup and plan formatting can delay comparison of human-defined options.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing planning tools can rerun validated models and scenario templates against checked data.
tasks.still_hard: Uncertain future conditions and conflicting conservation, supply and stakeholder goals require judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist can reject an apparently efficient scenario that rests on implausible assumptions or unacceptable trade-offs.

ambition.what: Reassess operating options as actual watershed conditions change.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2–5 for monitoring data, model access and operator consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: hydrological planning tools can repeat validated model scenarios and sensitivity calculations, while people choose objectives and operating strategies.

assumptions: All effort shares are provisional scenarios, not measured watershed-planning baselines.
An appropriate validated model and actual monitoring records already exist. Developing a new scientific model is outside this configuration estimate and must be separately counted if needed.
Human options and constraints originate in s1 and s2; the specialist captures the chosen rationale in s5 and actual plan in s6.
Native scenario functions first; no language model chooses operating rules or interprets missing compliance requirements.
The proposed strategy is saved for authorised governance, not automatically implemented. Same-system save has no saving.
research_questions: Which repeated scenario setup can be reused without hiding model uncertainty?

already_counted.description: Check final proposed strategy against chosen goals

incremental.description: Maintain source mappings, approved scenarios and model-version checks

approvals.approved_version: approved final proposed watershed strategy; changes return to s7

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross is 10 data-preparation hours +12 repeated scenario hours +2 plan-assembly hours =24. Three upkeep hours give central net 21%; five additional hours checking unusual hydrological conditions gives high 16%. Low zero if existing tools already cover this or no reusable validated model exists.
